1947, December 8
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, O. F. M. Cap.
SAINT FELIX MONASTERY. HUNTINGTON INDIANA.
December 8th, Feast of the Immaculate Conception. ,947.
Mrs. Charles D'Amico 379 Caler Avenue Seattle, Washington
My Dear Niece Dorothy:
God bless you this most cherished feast of our Blessed Mother Mary. I do hope she may bless you specially - you and yours.
However, to insure such a booned favor, we ought on our part try to find some way whereby specially to please her our so gracious blessed Mother. This we can hardly do better than by studying her life and trying to imitate her peerless practice of the Christian virtues - or any one of them - charity. pat- ience, purity, humility, temperance, etc.
Of course if we remember and keep in mind that the greates doctors of the Church and theologians are unanimous in their conviction that even at the very first instant of Mary's soul's conception she received greater and more abundent graces than all other creatures taken together -- as the brightest moon outshines all the stars -- and that even the highest seraphim can follow only at a shadowy distance her Christ-like practice of the virtues as she grew in wisdom and grace before god and men
(unfinished)
(Mrs. Dorothy D'Amico, daughter of Ella Casey Traynor)
